bullets.title: Middle East escalation drives oil to 3-month highs; Brent near $100, WTI +23% in a month
bullets.body: Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery (400k bpd capacity) and U.S. military destruction of three IRGC crude tankers in the Persian Gulf have driven WTI to new contract highs (~$93.90) and Brent near $100/barrel. Goldman Sachs warns of $120/barrel risk if attacks intensify; global markets are missing ~2mn bpd Russian products and ~2mn bpd Middle East products, with diesel crack spreads at record levels. An Iran-Oman shipping corridor deal is a possible diplomatic off-ramp but physical product scarcity could persist beyond any political settlement.

bullets.title: August CPI (Friday) is the pivotal macro event; September hike probability at 60%
bullets.body: With the Fed seen delivering 2 hikes by year-end and only 15bps priced for September, Friday's August CPI print is the decisive input for the 16-Sep FOMC decision. September rate hike probability currently sits at 60%; treasury and bund positioning is stretched (below -6 on a -10/+10 scale), meaning a benign print could trigger a meaningful short-covering rally in duration. UST 10-year yields are tracking toward a 4.87% target per Hedgeye, with the 10-year at ~4.79% pre-market.

bullets.title: Macro data reinforces 'Quad 2' regime: manufacturing at cycle high, labor firm, inflation sticky
bullets.body: ISM manufacturing expanded across 83.3% of industries—the highest level of the cycle—while the employment diffusion index hit a 4-year high of 61%. Unemployment claims near 200k support ~235k monthly payroll growth through year-end. Nominal GDP is running ~6% (3% real + 3% inflation), with global bond yields rising on growth rather than just oil; U.S. 10-year yields are projected near 5% by November 2027. CCC-B credit spreads have broken above the post-Covid peak, a historically leading indicator of stress.

bullets.title: NFIB small business optimism cools in August; profit trends reverse lower
bullets.body: NFIB headline fell 1.1 points to 98.7 in August after July's surge, with only 2 of 10 components improving vs. 8 in July. Profit trends dropped 3 points to net -19%, hiring plans fell 3 points to net 17%, and inflation remains the #1 cited problem at 16% of owners (tied with taxes). Credit conditions improved to best level since December 2024, with short-term loan rates falling to 7.5%.

bullets.title: Semiconductor upcycle accelerating: memory ASPs surging, AI demand supply-constrained through 2028
bullets.body: JPM raised its 2026 industry outlook to $1.73T (+118% YoY) and >$2T for 2027; UBS forecasts $2.43T in 2027 and $2.72T in 2028. DRAM ASPs are +259% YoY, NAND +344% YoY, with Samsung and SK Hynix inventories below 10 days of supply. Leading-edge wafer capacity (N3/N2) and HBM remain the primary bottlenecks, with supply-demand imbalance unlikely to ease before 2028. DDR5 RDIMM prices rose 8.1% W/W and 13.9% M/M as of Sep 1; B200 GPU rental prices up 27% W/W.

bullets.title: AI token consumption up 10x YTD; datacenter capex projected at $1.4T in 2027, $3T by 2030
bullets.body: Token demand is accelerating 10x YTD (vs. 4x last year) driven by agentic AI adoption, while token spend is up 12x Y/Y despite a 5% M/M price decline. AI datacenter power demand is projected at 1,000 TWh by 2028 (24% of 2025 U.S. consumption), with a power constraint inflection expected 2028-29. Datacenter capex is estimated at $1.4T in 2027 and $3.0T in 2030, requiring significant debt/equity issuance; GPU rental margins are reaching 50% gross with spot rates well above existing contracts.

bullets.title: Hedge funds net re-grossed into Mag 7 and US Tech/Semis at >1std; software heavily sold
bullets.body: Hedge funds net bought Mag 7 at +1.9 standard deviations and broad US Tech/Semis at >1.0std, fully reversing YTD de-grossing. Simultaneously, U.S. software is the most heavily sold factor at -1.6std as funds take profits on AI-resilient names. Re-grossing picked up +1.3z in the past week, the highest since late June, per JPM.

bullets.title: INTC +4.5% pre-market on Digitimes report of 10% PC CPU price hike; Northland upgrades to OP
bullets.body: Digitimes reported Intel PC CPU prices are set to rise another 10% on supply chain constraints, driving INTC up 4.3-4.7% pre-market. Northland Capital upgraded INTC to Outperform with a $120 PT (25% upside from $95.80). Jensen Huang declaring 'AGI has arrived' on OpenAI's Astra model is supporting the broader AI infrastructure narrative underpinning the move.

bullets.title: ASML wins High-NA EUV commitments from TSMC (2030) and Samsung (2028); could be 10-15% of sales
bullets.body: TSMC and Samsung have formally committed to adopt ASML's High-NA EUV tools, switching to 12-inch photomasks, with Samsung's commitment for 2028 and TSMC's for 2030. Citi's bull-case WFE guidance implies $163B/$224B/$286B in 2026/27/28 (37%/27% growth in 2027/28). ASML shares rose ~4% on the news.

bullets.title: NVDA/MediaTek $3.5B convertible bond deal seeds NVLink Fusion across custom ASIC ecosystem
bullets.body: NVIDIA and MediaTek announced a ~$3.5B convertible bond investment alongside a strategic partnership covering AI infrastructure, PCs, edge AI, and automotive. MediaTek's adoption of NVLink Fusion challenges AVGO and expands NVDA's architectural footprint into mid-range vehicles where QUALCOMM/MediaTek dominate. NVDA's strategic equity portfolio has grown to $99B (from $7B a year ago) as it backs AI-related companies with $40B+ in 2026 commitments to secure manufacturing access.

bullets.title: AI sovereignty and geopolitical tech fragmentation creating new capex and investment opportunities
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley frames AI capability as increasingly strategic for governments, with the risk of broader tech restrictions from geopolitical fragmentation opening opportunities across multiple sectors. Separately, Canada is moving to impose 15-50% retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods, and bipartisan datacenter opposition (PA Gov. Shapiro, TX Gov. Abbott) is slowing projects, with 69% of Americans opposing local AI datacenter siting.

bullets.title: Market transitioning from early to mid-cycle: software/services expected to outperform semis/hardware
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley sees the market transitioning from AI enablers (hardware/semis) to adopters, with software, financial services, insurance, and healthcare services expected to outperform. Core PCE is expected to fall to 3.1% from 3.3%, supporting a quality, asset-light rotation. SOX was down 18% in summer on high expectations and earnings deceleration; hardware is +1% while software is -4.50% over the past 5 days.

bullets.title: GS Communacopia Conference today; ORCL +5%, ADBE/ORCL report Thursday after close
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs's Communacopia tech conference kicks off today with keynotes from OpenAI, GOOGL, and AVGO. ORCL is up 5% pre-market on OpenAI Astra follow-through; ORCL regression analysis signals upside to OCI growth and RPO conversions but financing risk persists with CDS near record highs. ADBE and ORCL report Thursday after close; consensus EPS is $6.08/$1.73 on revenue of $6.69B/$19.13B respectively.

bullets.title: Apple foldable iPhone (iPhone Ultra) launches tomorrow; supply constrained to a few hundred units/day
bullets.body: Apple's Wednesday product event is expected to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max alongside the first foldable iPhone (iPhone Ultra), and potentially AirPods 5. iPhone Ultra production is reportedly constrained to only a few hundred units per day due to quality issues. Apple also signed a long-term NAND supply agreement with Kioxia.

bullets.title: Quantum stocks surge: IONQ raises guidance to $450-460M; RGTI and QBTS each secure $100M CHIPS Act funding
bullets.body: IONQ raised FY26 revenue guidance to $450-460M (including SkyWater) vs. prior $280-290M, driving shares up 7.2% pre-market. RGTI signed a $100M definitive agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce for superconducting quantum computing R&D, while QBTS finalized up to $100M in CHIPS Act funding. Both RGTI (+8.1%) and QBTS (+4.6%) are rallying on the news.

bullets.title: WTI up 23% in a month; copper at ATH; small caps underperforming as bond yields accelerate
bullets.body: Hedgeye is net short (6 shorts vs. 2 longs), long oil (OIH) and copper miners, short TLT/ZROZ/XLU. Russell 2000 is down 2.0% in the last month while large caps are up; UST 2-year yields are up 17bps and 10-year up 16bps over the same period. The S&P 500 immediate-term risk range is 7,615-7,772 with the 10-year yield range at 4.70-4.87%.

bullets.title: DOE closes $1.9B loan for NextEra's Duane Arnold nuclear restart; Google signs 25-year PPA
bullets.body: The DOE finalized up to a $1.9B conditional loan for the 615MW Duane Arnold nuclear facility restart in Iowa, expected by Q1 2029. Google signed a 25-year power purchase agreement for carbon-free nuclear energy from Duane Arnold to power its AI/cloud infrastructure. NextEra and Google already have ~3.5 GW in operation or contracted, with additional new nuclear generation being explored.

bullets.title: Housing market weakening: pending sales hit six-week low, mortgage rates back up to 6.71%
bullets.body: Pending home sales fell to -3.6% YoY (a six-week low and a near-10ppt swing from +6.3% in June), while new listings surged to the 79th percentile of historical readings at +7.95% YoY. The 30-year mortgage rate backed up 5bps to 6.71% (+21bps YoY), the largest weekly move in a month, widening the mortgage spread to 201bps. Purchase application volumes are at the 0th percentile of historical range.

bullets.title: JPM tactically cautious on equities but sees dips as buyable; EU hedges recommended
bullets.body: JPM moved to neutral/tactically cautious last Monday citing terminal G4 central bank rates, energy prices, politics, and the July/August tech rotation. Global equity dips are still expected to be bought—no risk is seen as large enough to end the cycle given solid revisions, accelerating GDP, and light positioning. EU equity index hedges are specifically recommended given ECB uncertainty and geopolitical exposure.

bullets.title: Bloom Energy added to S&P 500 (effective Sept 21); ~$11B in index inflows expected
bullets.body: BE was announced for S&P 500 inclusion effective September 21, representing approximately $11B in forced index inflows. Morgan Stanley maintains a constructive stance on on-site generation plays (BE) and powered shell plays (WULF, HUT) as solutions to AI datacenter power bottlenecks. HUBS also gained S&P MidCap 400 inclusion, rallying 2.1% pre-market.
